sections.h2: Ways to sell a house in Celina
sections.html:
Selling straight to a cash buyer is normally the fastest way out in Celina, because no one is waiting on a mortgage approval or a punch list. The slower routes can earn more on a house that is in good condition.

  • Go with an agent if the house shows well and you can wait on the buyer's lender.
  • Go it alone if you're at ease drafting the contract and vetting buyers.
  • Take cash if the house needs work, has a tenant, belongs to an estate, or has a fixed deadline.

sections.h2: Where Celina sits and why dates matter
sections.html:
Celina lies in northwestern Collin County on State Highway 289 and Farm Road 455, about fifteen miles northwest of McKinney and twelve miles north of Frisco. The town was established in 1879, named by a settler for his native Celina, Tennessee, and incorporated in 1907. The city now describes rapid growth that it wants to balance with the town's heritage.

With that much change, check the date on any survey, plat or permit. A document from a decade ago may describe a very different lot, street or utility layout.

Inside the city limits, any structure that is built, enlarged, altered, repaired, removed, converted, moved or demolished needs a permit from the Building Services Division. Residential permits go through the residential permit desk at (945) 362-9250 or permits@celina-tx.gov, at 112 N. Colorado St.

Celina residential permit rules

If you pulled a permit for a pool, a garage conversion or a roof and never closed it, call the permit desk before you list. An unfinished permit can delay a title company even when the work looks complete. The city also publishes policy sheets on residential fences, the irrigation ordinance, wood structure columns and brace shear wall fasteners, so ask which apply if you built or changed any of those.

sections.h2: Which appraisal district values my Celina house?
sections.html:
Property in Collin County is valued by the Collin Central Appraisal District. Its website covers a homestead exemption audit connected to Senate Bill 1801 and a tax transparency site that shows the taxing units on a bill. An address near a county line can sit on a different roll, so find the district named on your statement. Then check the exemptions on the account, the value history and the units listed.

Three state rules shape every Texas bill. Payment is due when the October bill arrives. Anything unpaid after January 31 is delinquent. The year's lien attaches on January 1. The first month of lateness costs a six percent penalty and one percent interest. A buyer's title review will turn up unpaid tax, so find out from your title company how this year's bill gets handled.

School districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead. Owners who are older or disabled get more school relief plus a tax ceiling, and a disabled veteran receives an exemption set by rating. The district's site links to its homestead information and its appraisal review board.

Your exemption stays with you, and the buyer who moves in applies for their own. Have your current exemptions in front of you when you talk about taxes, so the buyer knows what the bill looked like under your ownership.

Texas attaches different clocks to each of these.

  • Inheritance: probate of a will is open for four years after death. The small estate affidavit works only if assets other than homestead and exempt property total $75,000 or less. Heirs can also swear out an affidavit of heirship and file it with the clerk, though nobody has to accept it.
  • Tenants: the landlord serves a written notice, 3 days unless the lease says otherwise, then sues in justice court, with the hearing set 10 to 21 days after filing.
  • Foreclosure: the borrower can reinstate in the 20 days after the default notice, and courthouse auctions happen on first Tuesdays.

Before signing a contract, see a Texas attorney or the county clerk, and tell the buyer everything at the start.

The permit counter is open four days a week, so a trip to 112 N. Colorado St. on a Friday won't help. Call (945) 362-9250 or email permits@celina-tx.gov first and ask for the status of every permit tied to your address. Inspection requests close at 3:30 PM, so one made late in the day waits for the next. If a final inspection is all that stands between you and a closed permit, schedule it before you list and keep the result with the rest of your records.

New rules affect older paperwork, too. Since February 2026 applications and inspections follow the 2024 International Code Council codes, and permits filed after December 8, 2025 live in MGO Connect while earlier ones remain in MyGov. Know which system holds yours, so you can pull the record quickly when a title company or buyer asks. A record that is easy to produce tells a buyer the house has been looked after.

A buyer paying cash in Celina doesn't need a lender's appraisal or repair list, and doesn't wait for loan approval. What remains is clear title, a payoff on any loan, the year's property tax and any open permit. If the house is a rental, the lease comes along with it. If the seller is an heir, the buyer will want to see the probate paperwork or affidavit before agreeing on a date. Work through those items with the title company early, ideally before you accept an offer, and a closing within a few weeks is realistic.

sections.h2: Papers to collect before asking for offers
sections.html:
A folder of papers saves days.

  • The most recent tax statement and the appraisal district account number.
  • Any open permit number, and the final inspection record for finished work.
  • The mortgage payoff figure, if there is a loan.
  • Any HOA contact and dues balance.
  • Lease copies, if a tenant lives in the house.

faqs.q: How long does a Celina building permit stay valid?
faqs.a: It expires on the 181st day if no inspection has taken place or no progress has been shown. An application with no permit issued within 180 days is treated as abandoned. Call the residential permit desk at (945) 362-9250 for an exact status.

faqs.q: Do Celina homeowners pay a city tax separate from the county?
faqs.a: Texas has no state property tax, and each local unit that taxes your address sets its own rate. Your tax statement lists every unit. Call the tax office for rates before you estimate anything.

faqs.q: Is Celina in Collin County or Denton County?
faqs.a: Celina sits in northwestern Collin County, and the Collin Central Appraisal District values property there. Your own tax statement names the district that carries your parcel.

faqs.q: Can an heir sell a Celina house without full probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A muniment of title or small estate affidavit can work when the estate qualifies and the court approves. A probate attorney can confirm which fits.

faqs.q: Do repairs have to be finished before a Celina sale?
faqs.a: No. Many buyers purchase as-is. The main issue is an open permit, which you should disclose and, if possible, resolve with the city's permit desk first.
